learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to set up the differential equation for heat conduction for a volume element and solve it given local/temporal boundary conditions.
Students are able to apply dimensionless characteristic numbers of fluid mechanics to calculate the heat transfer coefficient using suitable Nusselt number correlations.

Students are able to graphically represent temperature profiles in heat exchangers depending on the flow direction and in the presence of phase change. Furthermore, methods for the design (LTD method) and verification (NTU method) of heat exchangers are known.
Students are able to explain the principles of electromagnetic heat radiation and apply them, assuming simplified model bodies, to determine heat transfer by radiation in solids.
Students are able to apply the knowledge acquired about the heat transport mechanisms covered in the lecture to the respective practical experiments.
